summary: Lane County butte above Oakridge: a lookout station was planned in June 1917 and a lookout was posted there that summer; no later record found.

events.note: Government trail under construction to the summit, where a lookout station was to be established (June 1917).
A lookout named Gus Ryker was posted on the butte in the days before August 3, 1917.
The lookout spotted smoke from a house roof in the valley below; Oakridge men put the fire out with a bucket brigade.

notes_for_editor: Only one hobbyist directory page (quoting 1917 Morning Register items) describes this butte; it names only 'National Forest', so agency is left out of facts. The Willamette history supports Oakridge as a ranger district but does not mention Bald Butte, so the link between the butte and that forest is inferred, not documented; check Willamette NF records before relying on it. Do not mix this record with the Fremont-Winema, Ochoco or Hood River Bald Buttes, which search results return too; the oregonhikers.org Bald Butte page is the Hood River site and was not used. Nothing after August 1917 is in the sources, and the record's status is unverified.
